chunks: Ibn Mahboub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Salih who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a slave who cut off the hand of a free man, and for him were three paralysed fingers from his hand. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is the value of the slave?' I said, 'Make it to be whatever you like'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the value of the slave was more than the wergild of the two correct fingers, and the three paralysed fingers, the one whose hand was cut off has to return to the master of the slave whatever was the remainder from the value, and seize the slave; and if he so desire to he can take the value of the two correct fingers and the three paralysed fingers'.

I said, 'And how much is the value of the two correct fingers along with the palm, and the three paralysed fingers?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The value of the two correct fingers along with the palm is two thousand Dirhams, and the value of the three paralysed fingers along with the palm is a thousand Dirhams, because it is the third from the wergild of the correct (fingers).'.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if it was such that the value of the slave is less than the wergild of the two correct fingers, and the three paralysed fingers, the slave would be handed over to the one whose hand was cut off, or his master has to ransom him, and he can take the slave'.

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for injury/death
key_terms.صَحِيح: Correct, sound, or healthy (referring to fingers)
key_terms.قِيمَة: Value or price (specifically of the slave in this context)

ai.seo_question: How is blood money calculated when a slave injures a free man's hand according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of 'ta'wil' (retaliatory compensation) where a slave injures a free man, establishing that the slave's market value serves as the baseline for determining whether the victim receives the slave or monetary diya. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the value of the slave and the specific valuation of hand injuries (two healthy fingers and three paralyzed ones), reflecting the nuanced application of Quranic principles of equality in retribution.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is the value of the slave?’ I said, ‘Make it to be whatever you<sup>asws</sup> like’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And if it was such that the value of the slave is less than the wergild of the two correct fingers, and the three paralysed fingers, the slave would be handed over to the one whose hand was cut off, or his master has to ransom him, and he can take the slave’.
